findings.title: IPv6 unspecified address not in denied_dst
findings.detail: always_denied.cidrs has 0.0.0.0/8 (squid would connect to its own loopback) but not its IPv6 twin ::/128; a web_public caller's AAAA of :: makes squid try [::]:80/443 in the proxy netns. Nothing listens there today. Add ::/128 (optionally ::ffff:0:0/96 as documentation).

findings.title: Hyper-V drift check reads rule names only
findings.detail: hyperv-firewall.ps1 keeps any rule with the right name and the ossctl.ps1 doctor PASS checks only names and Block defaults; neither validates protocol/ports/action/enabled nor enumerates other Allow rules for the WSL VMCreatorId. Require exactly the two ossbot rules (Outbound, Allow, Enabled, TCP, 443/80) and re-create rules whose properties differ.

findings.title: Unit seccomp confinement assumes no reachable user manager, unasserted
findings.detail: A unit that can reach its uid's systemd user manager can systemd-run --user an unfiltered process (AF_VSOCK to 2:50002 again). Closed today by ProtectHome=yes hiding /run/user and no linger for service uids, but neither is asserted. Assert ProtectHome in {yes, tmpfs} for every non-root unit in test_systemd_units.py, and Linger=no / no /run/user/<uid> for the five service uids in the surface test and doctor; record in threat-table row 41.

findings.title: Threat-table row 7 misstates who holds broad egress
findings.detail: Row 7 says only secretless callers hold shared-front-end categories, but the research pool and Hermes hold a Kiro key plus web_public (approved ADR-0005 design). Reword rows 7/36 so the accepted residual names the actual control (ADR-0017 key out of tool reach, output key scans); CR-002 'open' adds agent-llm to this set.

findings.title: io_uring control window in the surface test has no dead-man restore
findings.detail: The test stops ossbot-watchdog.timer and sets kernel.io_uring_disabled=0; the EXIT trap does not run on SIGKILL or wsl --terminate, leaving io_uring enabled and drift monitoring off until the timer is started or the next boot. Arm a root systemd-run --on-active=90 job that restores the sysctl and starts the timer before the write, and cancel it after the restore.
